questions.q: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of $x^{2}-a x+b=0$ and if $\alpha^{\mathrm{n}}+\beta^{\mathrm{n}}=\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{n}}$, then
questions.solution:
Multiplying $x^{2}-a x+b=0$ by $x^{n-1}$, we get $x^{n+1}-a x^{n}+b x^{n-1}=0\alpha, \beta$ are roots of $x^{2}-a x+b=0$, therefore they will satisfy (i).
Also, $\alpha^{n+1}-a \alpha^{n}+b \alpha^{n-1}=0$ ...(ii)
and $\beta^{\mathrm{n}+1}-\mathrm{a} \beta^{\mathrm{n}}+\mathrm{b} \beta^{\mathrm{n}-1}=0$ ...(iii)
On adding eqs. (ii) and (iii), we get
$\begin{array}{l}
\left(\alpha^{\mathrm{n}+1}+\beta^{\mathrm{n}+1}\right)-\mathrm{a}\left(\alpha^{\mathrm{n}}+\beta^{\mathrm{n}}\right) \\
\quad+\mathrm{b}\left(\alpha^{\mathrm{n}-1}+\beta^{(\mathrm{n}-1)}\right)=0 \\
\Rightarrow \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{n}+1}-\mathrm{aV}_{\mathrm{n}}+\mathrm{bV}_{\mathrm{n}-1}=0\left(\because \alpha^{\mathrm{n}}+\beta^{\mathrm{n}}=\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{n}}\right) \\
\Rightarrow \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{n}+1}=\mathrm{aV}_{\mathrm{n}}-\mathrm{bV}_{\mathrm{n}-1}
\end{array}$

S_n & =\frac{n\left(n^2-1\right)(n+2)}{4} \\

questions.q: An equation of the plane passing through the line of intersection of the planes $x+y+z=6$ and $2 \mathrm{x}+3 \mathrm{y}+4 \mathrm{z}+5=0$ and passing through $(1,1,1)$ is
questions.solution:
The equation of the plane through the line of intersection of the given planes is $(x+y+z-6)+\lambda(2 x+3 y+4 z+5)=0$
If equation (1) passes through $(1,1,1)$, we have
$-3+14 \lambda=0 \Rightarrow \lambda=\frac{3}{14}$
Putting $\lambda=\frac{3}{14}$ in $(1)$, we obtain the equation of the required plane as
$\begin{array}{l}
(x+y+z-6)+\frac{3}{14}(2 x+3 y+4 z+5)=0 \\
\Rightarrow 20 x+23 y+26 z-69=0
\end{array}$
